rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who affirm God as Lord and remain upright join tawhid, the culmination of knowledge, to upright practice, the culmination of action.
rows.anchor: جمعوا بين التوحيد الذي هو خلاصة العلم والإستقامة في الأمور التي هي منتهى العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence marker thumma indicates that action ranks after tawhid and that its validity depends on tawhid.
rows.anchor: وثم للدلالة على تأخر رتبة العمل وتوقف اعتباره على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful have no fear of an approaching harm and no grief over a lost good; the fāʾ works because the preceding noun carries a conditional sense.
rows.anchor: من لحوق مكروه. { ولا هم يحزنون } على فوات محبوب، والفاء لتضمن الاسم معنى الشرط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is their lasting reward for acquiring intellectual and practical virtues.
rows.anchor: من اكتساب الفضائل العلمية والعملية، وخالدين حال من المستكن في أصحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, “abiding” is a circumstantial qualifier of the implicit subject in “companions,” and jazāʾ is a verbal noun for an implied “they were recompensed.”
rows.anchor: وخالدين حال من المستكن في أصحاب وجزاء مصدر لفعل دل عليه الكلام

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read iḥsānan in place of ḥusnan in the command to treat parents well.
rows.anchor: ووصينا الإنسن بوالديه حسنا } وقرأ الكوفيون «إحسانا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ḥusnan can mean that the instruction itself is good.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { حسنا } أي إيصاء { حسنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother bears and delivers the child with hardship; the phrase can mean possessing hardship or carrying a hardship-laden pregnancy.
rows.anchor: { حملته أمه كرها ووضعته كرها } ذات كره أو حملا ذا كره وهو المشقة

rows.speaker: الحجازيان وأبو عمرو وهشام
rows.claim: These readers pronounce kurhan with fatḥa; Bayḍāwī treats fatḥa and ḍamma as dialect forms, while another view makes the ḍamma a noun and the fatḥa a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان وأبو عمرو وهشام بالفتح وهما لغتان كالفقر والفقر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaml and fiṣāl refer to the periods of pregnancy and weaning; fiṣāl means weaning, supported by Yaʿqūb’s reading faṣl.
rows.anchor: والفصال الفطام ويدل عليه قراءة يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fiṣāl denotes its appointed time, meaning the completed nursing period that ends at that time.
rows.anchor: أو وقته والمراد به الرضاع التام المنتهى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line compares every living being’s allotted lifetime with the point when its term ends, illustrating the duration sense of amad.
rows.anchor: كل حي مستكمل عدة العم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thirty months describe the full burden a mother bears in raising a child, intensifying the command to care for her.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك بيان لما تكابده الأم في تربية الولد مبالغة في التوصية بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes a six-month minimum pregnancy: subtract the two complete nursing years stated in 2:233 from thirty months; doctors also hold this view.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن أقل مدة الحمل ستة أشهر لأنه إذا حط منه الفصال حولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The minimum pregnancy and maximum nursing periods are specified because they are measurable and determine rules of lineage and breastfeeding.
rows.anchor: ولعل تخصيص أقل الحمل وأكثر الرضاع لانضباطهما وتحقق ارتباط حكم النسب والرضاع بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching full strength means becoming mature and having strength and reason fully established.
rows.anchor: إذا اكتهل واستحكم قوته وعقله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view says no prophet was commissioned before the age of forty.
rows.anchor: قيل لم يبعث نبي إلا بعد الأربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awziʿnī means “inspire me”; Bayḍāwī relates its root sense to making someone ardently attached to something.
rows.anchor: ألهمني وأصله أولعني من أوزعته بكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing sought in gratitude can mean the blessing of religion or all blessings; this fits a report that the verse was revealed about Abū Bakr, the only Emigrant or Helper Muslim whose parents were both Muslim.
rows.anchor: يعني نعمة الدين أو ما يعمها وغيرها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “righteous deed” magnifies the deed or specifies a kind that wins God’s approval.
rows.anchor: نكرة للتعظيم أو لأنه أراد نوعا من الجنس يستجلب رضا الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks that righteousness run through the speaker’s descendants and become firmly rooted among them; Bayḍāwī cites a poem as a parallel.
rows.anchor: واجعل لي الصلاح ساريا في ذريتي راسخا فيهم ونحوه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance here is turning away from what God disapproves or from whatever distracts one from Him.
rows.anchor: عما لا ترضاه أو يشغل عنك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the Muslims means being sincerely devoted to God.
rows.anchor: وإني من المسلمين } المخلصين لك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Obedience and a proper word” can be an independent statement commanding obedience or a statement that obedience and proper speech are better for them.
rows.anchor: استئناف أي أمرهم { طاعة }

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: In Ubayy’s reading, the phrase is reported speech: “they say: obedience.”
rows.anchor: أو حكاية قولهم لقراءة أبي «يقولون طاعة».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the matter is decided, it means the affair has become serious; attributing the decision to the affair is figurative, and the adverb has an omitted governing verb.
rows.anchor: أي جد وهو لأصحاب الأمر، وإسناده إليه مجاز وعامل الظرف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If they were truthful” may refer to their claimed eagerness for fighting or their claimed faith.
rows.anchor: فيما زعموا من الحرص على الجهاد أو الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether one should expect them, if put in charge of people, to spread corruption and sever kinship.
rows.anchor: فهل يتوقع منكم. { إن توليتم } أمور الناس وتأمرتم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, taking charge means turning away from Islam.
rows.anchor: أو أعرضتم وتوليتم عن الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption and cutting kinship can mean fighting over rule, or returning to pre-Islamic raiding and fighting among relatives.
rows.anchor: تناحرا على الولاية وتجاذبا لها، أو رجوعا إلى ما كنتم عليه في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their weak faith and worldly greed make corruption and severing family ties an expected outcome; the question rebukes those who know their condition.
rows.anchor: لضعفهم في الدين وحرصهم على الدنيا أحقاء بأن يتوقع ذلك منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hijazi usage ʿasaytum takes an attached pronoun and its predicate is “that you corrupt”; the conditional phrase is parenthetical, while Tamīm does not attach that pronoun.
rows.anchor: وهذا على لغة الحجاز فإن بني تميم لا يلحقون الضمير به وخبره { أن تفسدوا }

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the verb as “if you are placed under rulers,” meaning you would join oppressive rulers in corruption and severing kin.
rows.anchor: أي إن تولاكم ظلمة خرجتم معهم وساعدتموهم في الإفساد وقطيعة الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading has taqṭaʿū from the form meaning “be severed” rather than the form meaning “cut.”
rows.anchor: { وتقطعوا } من القطع، وقرىء { تقطعوا } من التقطع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah is Medinan, revealed as the Messenger returned from al-Ḥudaybiyya, and contains twenty-nine verses.
rows.anchor: مدنية نزلت في مرجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الحديبية وآيها تسع وعشرون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “clear opening” promises the conquest of Mecca; the past tense presents it as certain.
rows.anchor: وعد بفتح مكة، والتعبير عنه بالماضي لتحققه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the opening refers to victories that occurred that year, including Khaybar and Fadak.
rows.anchor: أو بما اتفق له في تلك السنة كفتح خيبر وفدك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyya: the polytheists sought peace after the Prophet gained the upper hand, and the treaty enabled Mecca’s conquest, further campaigns, and many conversions.
rows.anchor: أو إخبار عن صلح الحديبية وإنما سماه فتحا لأنه كان بعد ظهوره على المشركين حتى سألوا الصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At al-Ḥudaybiyya, its water had run out; after the Prophet rinsed and spat into it, water flowed until everyone with him drank.
rows.anchor: وظهر له في الحديبية آية عظيمة وهي أنه نزح ماؤها بالكلية فتمضمض ثم مجه فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the opening is the Romans’ victory over the Persians that year, already described as a victory for the Prophet in Sūrat al-Rūm.
rows.anchor: أو فتح الروم فإنهم غلبوا الفرس في تلك السنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes fatḥ as a decree: God decreed that the Prophet would enter Mecca the following year.
rows.anchor: وقيل الفتح بمعنى القضاء أي قضينا لك أن تدخل مكة من قابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness is a consequence and purpose of the opening: jihad removes shirk, raises the religion, gradually brings deficient souls to willing perfection, and frees the oppressed.
rows.anchor: علة للفتح من حيث إنه مسبب عن جهاد الكفار والسعي في إزاحة الشرك وإعلاء الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What preceded and followed of your sin” means every lapse for which you could rightly be reproached.
rows.anchor: جميع ما فرط منك مما يصح أن تعاتب عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completes His blessing by exalting the religion and joining kingship to prophethood.
rows.anchor: بإعلاء الدين وضم الملك إلى النبوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the way of conveying the message and carrying out the duties of leadership.
rows.anchor: في تبليغ الرسالة وإقامة مراسم الرئاسة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mighty victory is one that contains strength and protection, or one that makes its beneficiary mighty; the adjective is transferred figuratively for emphasis.
rows.anchor: نصرا فيه عز ومنعة، أو يعز به المنصور فوصف بوصفه مبالغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakīna is steadiness and reassurance in believers’ hearts, enabling them to stand firm where people are anxious and feet slip.
rows.anchor: الثبات والطمأنينة. { في قلوب المؤمنين } حتى ثبتوا حيث تقلق النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing faith can mean certainty added to certainty through firm belief and settled hearts.
rows.anchor: يقينا مع يقينهم برسوخ العقيدة واطمئنان النفس عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the reassurance concerns what the Messenger brought, so believers increase in faith in the revealed laws alongside faith in God and the Last Day.
rows.anchor: أو نزل فيها السكون إلى ما جاء به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ليزدادوا إيمانا بالشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs the hosts of heaven and earth, sometimes setting them against one another and sometimes bringing peace, as His wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: يدبر أمرها فيسلط بعضها على بعض تارة ويوقع فيما بينهم السلم أخرى كما تقتضيه حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what serves people’s interests and is wise in what He decrees and directs.
rows.anchor: بالمصالح. { حكيما } فيما يقدر ويدبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer is that recompense will certainly occur: God’s power to produce wonders contrary to nature proves His power to resurrect for the promised judgment; dīn means recompense and wāqiʿ means realized.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم كأنه استدل باقتداره على هذه الأشياء العجيبة المخالفة لمقتضى الطبيعة على اقتداره على البعث للجزاء الموعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥubuk may mean visible paths, such as the courses of the planets, or conceptual paths followed by thinkers toward knowledge.
rows.anchor: والمراد إما الطرائق المحسوسة التي هي مسير الكواكب أو المعقولة التي يسلكها النظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the paths are the stars themselves or the pathways with which they adorn the sky, like patterns woven into decorated cloth.
rows.anchor: أو النجوم فإن لها طرائق أو أنها تزينها كما يزين الموشي طرائق الوشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥubuk is pluralized either as ḥabīka, like ṭarīqa/ṭuruq, or as ḥibāk, like mithāl/mithl.
rows.anchor: جمع حبيكة كطريقة وطرق أو حباك كمثال ومثل

rows.speaker: قراءات غير مسماة
rows.claim: The word ḥubuk is reported with several vowel patterns: sukūn, forms like al-ibil, al-silk, al-jabal, al-naʿam, and al-barq.
rows.anchor: وقرىء « الحبك» بالسكون و «الحبك » كالإبل و« الحبك » كالسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conflicting statements concern the Messenger, whom they variously call a poet, sorcerer, or madman; alternatives are that the dispute concerns the Qurʾān, Resurrection, or religion.
rows.anchor: في الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو قولهم تارة أنه { شاعر } وتارة أنه { سحر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s rhetorical point is to liken their mutually distant and incompatible claims to the heavens’ paths, whose destinations also differ.
rows.anchor: ولعل النكتة في هذا القسم تشبيه أقوالهم في اختلافها وتنافي أغراضها بطرائق السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vague description of what covered the lote tree magnifies it as so abundant that no description or count can encompass it.
rows.anchor: تعظيم وتكثير لما يغشاها بحيث لا يكتنهها نعت ولا يحصيها عد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says that a vast multitude of angels worshipped God at the lote tree.
rows.anchor: وقيل يغشاها الجم الغفير من الملائكة يعبدون الله عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s gaze neither deviated from what he saw nor exceeded it; he fixed it accurately and with certainty.
rows.anchor: ما مال بصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عما رآه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, his gaze did not turn from the wonders he was commanded to see or go beyond them.
rows.anchor: أو ما عدل عن رؤية العجائب التي أمر برؤيتها وما جاوزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Night Journey and ascent, the Prophet saw great signs and wonders of the angelic and unseen realms.
rows.anchor: لقد رأى من آياته وعجائبه الملكية والملكوتية ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the greatest sign with the object referred to in the account of what he saw.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل إنها المعنية بما { رأى }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, al-kubrā may modify āyāt with an omitted object, or min may be redundant.
rows.anchor: { الكبرى } صفة لل { ءايت } على أن المفعول محذوف أي شيئا من آيات ربه أو { من } مزيدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Lāt was an idol of Thaqīf at Ṭāʾif or Quraysh at Nakhlah; its name is linked to their circling it in worship.
rows.anchor: فاللات كانت لثقيف بالطائف أو لقريش بنخلة وهي فعلة من لوى لأنهم كانوا يلوون عليها

rows.speaker: هبة الله عن البزي ورويس عن يعقوب
rows.claim: These readers double the tāʾ in al-Lāt; an explanation derives the name from a man who kneaded flour with ghee and fed pilgrims, whose image was worshipped.
rows.anchor: وقرأ هبة الله عن البزي ورويس عن يعقوب«اللت» بالتشديد على أنه سمي به لأنه صورة رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿUzzā was a tree worshipped by Ghatafān; the Prophet sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to cut it down, and its name is the feminine of al-aʿazz.
rows.anchor: { والعزى } بالتشديد سمرة لغطفان كانوا يعبدونها فبعث إليها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خالد بن الوليد فقطعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāt was a stone of Hudhayl and Khuzāʿa, or of Thaqīf; the name may derive from cutting because sacrifices were made there.
rows.anchor: { ومنوة } صخرة كانت لهذيل وخزاعة أو لثقيف وهي فعلة من مناه إذا قطعه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads Manāh, deriving the name from seeking rain through the stars at that idol.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير { مناة } وهي مفعلة من النوء فإنهم كانوا يستمطرون الأنواء عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two adjectives “third” and “other” reinforce one another, like the wording in 6:38; alternatively, al-ukhrā marks lower rank.
rows.anchor: وقوله { الثالثة الأخرى } صفتان للتأكيد كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes assigning sons to God while claiming daughters for themselves, which they disdain.
rows.anchor: إنكار لقولهم الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols may be inhabited by female jinn whom the idolaters regarded as God’s daughters, or they may represent angelic forms.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأصنام استوطنها جنيات هن بناته، أو هياكل الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the syntax, the phrase is the second object of “Have you considered?”
rows.anchor: وهو المفعول الثاني لقوله { أفرءيتم }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division is unjust: ḍīzā derives from injustice, with its vowel changed to preserve the yāʾ because fuʿlā with kasra does not occur as an adjective.
rows.anchor: جائرة حيث جعلتم له ما تستنكفون منه وهي فعلى من الضيز وهو الجور

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word with hamza, deriving it from ḍaʾazahu, “he wronged him,” and using the verbal noun adjectivally.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير بالهمز من ضأزه إذا ظلمه على أنه مصدر نعت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “they” may refer to idols: they are names applied as gods, though they contain no reality of divinity.
rows.anchor: الضمير للأصنام أي ما هي باعتبار الألوهية إلا أسماء تطلقونها عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the attributes they assign the idols, such as being gods, daughters, and intercessors.
rows.anchor: أو للصفة التي تصفونها بها من كونها آلهة وبنات وشفعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the names Lat, ʿUzzā, and Manāt, which they chose to imply worship-worthiness, power, or entitlement to sacrifice.
rows.anchor: أو للأسماء المذكورة فإنهم كانوا يطلقون اللات عليها باعتبار استحقاقها للعكوف على عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You named them” means that you assigned those names to the idols.
rows.anchor: مناة لاعتقادهم أنها تستحق أن يتقرب إليها بالقرابين. { سميتموها } سميتم بها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They and their forefathers assigned the names according to their desires.
rows.anchor: { أنتم وءاباؤكم } بهواكم. { ما أنزل الله بها من سلطن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols have no revealed proof or warrant supporting the names given them.
rows.anchor: من سلطن } برهان تتعلقون به. { إن يتبعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with tāʾ instead of yāʾ is also reported for “they follow.”
rows.anchor: { إن يتبعون } وقرىء بالتاء. { إلا الظن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their belief is conjecture: an unfounded supposition sustained by imitation and a false sense that their practice is true.
rows.anchor: { إلا الظن } إلا توهم أن ما هم عليه حق تقليدا وتوهما باطلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They follow what their own selves desire.
rows.anchor: { وما تهوى الأنفس } وما تشتهيه أنفسهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance that came from their Lord means either the Messenger or the Book, which they abandoned.
rows.anchor: { ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى } الرسول أو الكتاب فتركوه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected am introduces a rejecting question: no person receives everything he wishes; the context denies hope in idol intercession and claims of special favor or status.
rows.anchor: { أم للإنسن ما تمنى } { أم } منقطعة ومعنى الهمزة فيها الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns the Hereafter and this world, giving from either to whomever He wills; no one can dictate to Him.
rows.anchor: { فلله الأخرة والأولى } يعطي منهما ما يشاء لمن يريد وليس لأحد أن يتحكم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah is variously described as Meccan, Medinan, or partly each, and it has seventy-eight verses.
rows.anchor: مكية أو مدنية أو متبعضة وآيها ثمان وسبعون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sūrah enumerates worldly and otherworldly blessings, it opens with the name al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: لما كانت السورة مقصورة على تعداد النعم الدنيوية والآخروية صدرها ب { الرحمن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is presented first as the greatest religious blessing: it grounds religion and law, is the most precious book, and by its inimitability and comprehensive content validates its message.
rows.anchor: إنعامه بالقرآن وتنزيله وتعليمه، فإنه أساس الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation and speech, which distinguishes people from animals, equip them to receive revelation, recognize truth, and learn the law.
rows.anchor: إيماء بأن خلق البشر وما يميز به عن سائر الحيوان من البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three clauses are unjoined reports about al-Raḥmān because they follow the form of an enumerated list.
rows.anchor: وإخلاء الجمل الثلاث التي هي أخبار مترادفة ل { الرحمن } عن العاطف لمجيئها على نهج التعديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The houris are secluded in their tents, like women sheltered in private quarters, or their glances are restricted to their husbands.
rows.anchor: قصرن في خدورهن، يقال امرأة قصيرة وقصورة ومقصورة أي مخدرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention that neither human nor jinn touched them before is linked to the houris of the two earlier gardens, whose description indicates this pairing.
rows.anchor: كحور الأولين وهم أصحاب الجنتين فإنهما يدلان عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafraf may mean cushions or pillows, or a type of rug, tent hem, or any broad cloth.
rows.anchor: وسائد أو نمارق جمع رفرفة. وقيل الرفرف ضرب من البسط أو ذيل الخيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbqarī derives from ʿAbqar, which Arabs imagined as a land of jinn; they used it for anything wondrous, and ḥisān is pluralized to agree with the collective sense.
rows.anchor: العبقري منسوب إلى عبقر، تزعم العرب أنه اسم بلد للجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s name is exalted because it applies to His essence; if the name is exalted, the essence is all the more so.
rows.anchor: تبرك اسم ربك } تعالى اسمه من حيث إنه مطلق على ذاته فما ظنك لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ism means attribute, or it is an extra word, as in the cited line about the greeting of peace after a year.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاسم بمعنى الصفة أو مقحم كما في قوله:

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads dhū in the nominative as an adjective of the word ism.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بالرفع صفة للاسم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever recites Sūrat al-Raḥmān has fulfilled gratitude for God’s blessings.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanzīl is a third or fourth adjective for the Qurʾān and is a verbal noun used adjectivally; another reading puts it in the accusative as tanẓīlan.
rows.anchor: صفة ثالثة أو رابعة للقرآن، وهو مصدر نعت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “discourse” is the Qurʾān; being mudhinūn means treating it laxly or neglectfully, as one who softens his stance.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن. { أنتم مدهنون } متهاونون به كمن يدهن في الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq here means gratitude for provision, and making it denial means denying its giver by attributing provision to the stars.
rows.anchor: أي شكر رزقكم. { أنكم تكذبون } أي بمانحه حيث تنسبونه إلى الأنواء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “your gratitude”; this can mean repaying the Qurʾān’s blessing by denying it as magic or poetry, or denying that rain comes from God by attributing it to stars.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «شكركم» أي تجعلون شكركم لنعمة القرآن أنكم تكذبون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one whose soul reaches the throat is the dying person.
rows.anchor: { فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم } أي النفس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You then look on” describes the condition of those around the dying person, with the wāw marking a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: حالكم، والخطاب لمن حول المحتضر والواو للحال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer in the sense of knowing more; knowledge is the strongest means of access, yet the onlookers cannot perceive what is happening to the dying person.
rows.anchor: { ونحن أقرب } أي ونحن أعلم. { إليه } إلى المحتضر. { منكم } عبر عن العلم بالقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being “not under dīn” can mean not facing recompense on Judgment Day, or not being owned and subdued; the root conveys abasement and submission.
rows.anchor: أي مجزيين يوم القيامة أو مملوكين مقهورين من دانه إذا أذله واستعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return it” means return the soul to its abode; the two repeated falawlā clauses emphasize the challenge and, with their clauses, indicate the conditional answer.
rows.anchor: { ترجعونها } ترجعون النفس إلى مقرها وهو عامل الظرف والمحضض عليه ب { فلولا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is: if, as your denial suggests, you are neither subject to God nor recompensed, then return souls to bodies after they reach the throat and prove your false claims.
rows.anchor: وهي بما في حيزها دليل جواب الشرط، والمعنى إن كنتم غير مملوكين مجزيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “if you are truthful” means truthful in your false claims.
rows.anchor: { إن كنتم صدقين } في أباطيلكم { فلولا } ترجعون الأرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deceased who is among the ones brought near is one of the foremost.
rows.anchor: أي إن كان المتوفى من السابقين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūḥ can mean rest and relief, mercy as the cause of the recipient’s life, or everlasting life.
rows.anchor: { فروح } فله استراحة وقرىء «فروح» بالضم وفسر بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayḥān means good provision, and the garden is one of bliss and enjoyment.
rows.anchor: ورزق طيب. { وجنة نعيم } ذات تنعم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Fire and the Garden are unequal: those who perfected their souls merit the Garden, while those who ruined them deserve the Fire; the Garden’s people are the winners.
rows.anchor: الذين استكملوا نفوسهم فاستأهلوا الجنة والذين استمهنوها فاستحقوا النار

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī says his legal school uses this verse as evidence that a Muslim is not executed in retaliation for a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: واحتج به أصحابنا على أن المسلم لا يقتل بالكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain passage is an illustrative fiction, as with the trust passage in 33:72; the following verse says such parables are given so people reflect.
rows.anchor: تمثيل وتخييل كما مر في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain image rebukes people for failing to humble themselves while reciting the Qurʾān, owing to hard hearts and little reflection; taṣaddaʿ means splitting.
rows.anchor: والمراد توبيخ الإنسان على عدم تخشعه عند تلاوة القرآن

rows.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
rows.claim: A reading has muṣaddaʿan with assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «مصدعا» على الإدغام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen may mean holy substances and their states, while the seen means bodies and their attributes; other pairs are nonexistent and existent, secret and public, or this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ما غاب عن الحس من الجواهر القدسية وأحوالها، وما حضر له من الأجرام وأعراضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the All-Merciful, the Merciful.
rows.anchor: هو الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s pledge was revealed on the day of the conquest, after the Prophet finished pledging the men and turned to the women.
rows.anchor: نزلت يوم الفتح فإنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لما فرغ من بيعة الرجال أخذ في بيعة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They will not kill their children” refers to burying daughters alive.
rows.anchor: ولا يقتلن أولدهن } يريد وأد البنات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction to what is right, though the Messenger commands only what is right, teaches that no created being may be obeyed in disobedience to the Creator.
rows.anchor: والتقييد بالمعروف مع أن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يأمر إلا به تنبيه على أنه لا يجوز طاعة مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is to accept the women’s pledge by undertaking reward for their fulfillment of these conditions.
rows.anchor: إذا بايعنك بضمان الثواب على الوفاء بهذه الأشياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those under God’s anger may mean all disbelievers or the Jews.
rows.anchor: لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم } يعني عامة الكفار أو اليهود.

rows.speaker: رواية غير مسماة
rows.claim: A report says the verse concerned poor Muslims who kept ties with Jews to obtain their fruit.
rows.anchor: إذ روي أنها نزلت في بعض فقراء المسلمين كانوا يواصلون اليهود ليصيبوا من ثمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers have despaired of the Hereafter because they deny it, or because they know they have no share after defying the Messenger described and supported by signs in the Torah.
rows.anchor: { قد يئسوا من الآخرة } لكفرهم بها أو لعلمهم بأنهم لاحظ لهم فيها لعنادهم الرسول المنعوت في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers despair that the dead will be raised, rewarded, or benefit them; on the first reading, “disbelievers” replaces a pronoun to show that their disbelief causes despair.
rows.anchor: كما يئس الكفر من أصحب القبور } أن يبعثوا أو يثابوا أو ينالهم خير منهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that believing men and women who recite Sūrat al-Mumtaḥana will have intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الممتحنة كان له المؤمنون والمؤمنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are layered one above another; ṭibāqan is either a verbal noun used adjectivally, a construction meaning “layered,” or an adjective meaning “possessing layers.”
rows.anchor: مطابقة بعضها فوق بعض مصدر طابقت النعل إذا خلطتها طبقا على طبق وصف به

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read tafāwut as tafawwut; both words mean discrepancy and lack of proportion.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «من تفوت» ومعناهما واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafāwut implies that each of two mismatched things lacks something present in the other; the phrase describes creation without inconsistency.
rows.anchor: وهو الاختلاف وعدم التناسب من الفوت كأن كلا من المتفاوتين فات عنه بعض ما في الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The creation of the All-Merciful” replaces a pronoun to magnify God’s power and signal that these heavens are a merciful gift containing countless blessings.
rows.anchor: وضع فيها خلق الرحمن موضع الضمير للتعظيم، والإشعار بأنه تعالى يخلق مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be directed to the Prophet or to every addressee.
rows.anchor: والخطاب فيها للرسول أو لكل مخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Look again” follows as a consequence: after looking repeatedly, inspect the heavens once more to see their proportion and completeness.
rows.anchor: متعلق به على معنى التسبب أي قد نظرت إليها مرارا فانظر إليها مرة أخرى متأملا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Futūr means fissures; here it means flaws, from the verb for splitting something open.
rows.anchor: وال { فطور } الشقوق والمراد الخلل من فطره إذا شقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what is hidden and public because He created things according to His wisdom; alternatively, the question means that the Creator surely knows His creatures.
rows.anchor: ألا يعلم السر والجهر من أوجد الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Laṭīf al-Khabīr describes knowledge that reaches both what is manifest in creation and what is hidden.
rows.anchor: المتوصل علمه إلى ما ظهر من خلقه وما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says idolaters privately discussed matters, then God informed His Messenger; the verse exposes their ignorance in thinking their speech escaped God.
rows.anchor: روي: أن المشركين كانوا يتكلمون فيما بينهم بأشياء، فيخبر الله بها رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth soft and easy for people to travel across.
rows.anchor: لينة يسهل لكم السلوك فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manākib may mean the earth’s sides or its mountains.
rows.anchor: في جوانبها أو جبالها، وهو مثل لفرط التذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking on the earth’s “shoulders” illustrates its extreme subduing: a camel’s shoulder resists being trodden, so if people can walk on the earth’s shoulders nothing remains untamed.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل لفرط التذليل فإن منكب البعير ينبو عن أن يطأه الراكب ولا يتذلل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should seek sustenance from God’s blessings, then return to Him for resurrection, when He will ask how they gave thanks.
rows.anchor: والتمسوا من نعم الله. { وإليه النشور } المرجع فيسألكم عن شكر ما أنعم عليكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds spread their wings in flight, aligning their leading feathers in the air.
rows.anchor: باسطات أجنحتهن في الجو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fold their wings periodically while beating their sides; the shift to a verb form distinguishes this occasional movement from the basic act of flight.
rows.anchor: { ويقبضن } ويضممنها إذا ضربن بها جنوبهن وقتا بعد وقت للاستظهار به على التحريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The All-Merciful alone keeps birds aloft contrary to nature by creating forms and properties suited to moving through air.
rows.anchor: { ما يمسكهن } في الجو على خلاف الطبع. { إلا الرحمن } الشامل رحمته كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees everything and knows how to create marvels and direct wonders.
rows.anchor: { إنه بكل شىء بصير } يعلم كيف يخلق الغرائب ويدبر العجائب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether people have considered these works and learned God can punish them with a collapse or a shower of stones; if punishment came, no army could defend them, as in 21:43.
rows.anchor: على معنى أو لم تنظروا في أمثال هذه الصنائع، فلم تعلموا قدرتنا على تعذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording asks who could defend them to suggest they believe some protector exists; the verse concludes that disbelievers rely on delusion.
rows.anchor: إشعارا بأنهم اعتقدوا هذا القسم، و { من } مبتدأ و { هذا } خبره و { الذى } بصلته صفته و { ينصركم } وصف ل { جند } محمول على لفظه. { إن الكفرون إلا في غرور } لا معتمد لهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God withholds rain and the other causes that bring food to people, no one else can provide for them.
rows.anchor: بإمساك المطر وسائر الأسباب المخلصة والموصلة له إليكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persisted in defiant resistance and fled from the truth because their natures recoiled from it.
rows.anchor: { بل لجوا } تمادوا. { فى عتو } عناد. { ونفور } شراد عن الحق لتنفر طباعهم عنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb akabba is an unusual form; it means becoming one who has fallen, like aqshaʿa means becoming cloudless, rather than being the passive of kabba.
rows.anchor: يقال كببته فأكب وهو من الغرائب كقشع الله السحاب فأقشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true passive forms are ankabba and inqašaʿa; mukib describes someone who repeatedly stumbles and falls face-first on a rough, uneven road.
rows.anchor: بل المطاوع لهما أنكب وانقشع، ومعنى { مكبا } أنه يعثر كل ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upright walker moves safely without stumbling on a straight, even path; the contrast depicts the disbeliever and monotheist as travelers on two religions.
rows.anchor: { أمن يمشى سويا } قائما سالما من العثار. { على صرط مستقيم } مستوي الأجزاء والجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rough route is left implicit to suggest that the polytheist’s way scarcely deserves to be called a path.
rows.anchor: ولعل الاكتفاء بما في الكب من الدلالة على حال المسلك للإشعار بأن ما عليه المشرك لا يستأهل أن يسمى طريقا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the face-down person is blind and stumbles, while the upright walker can see.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمكب الأعمى فإنه يتعسف فينكب وبالسوي البصير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the first person is resurrected face-first toward the Fire, while the upright one is resurrected on his feet toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل من { يمشى مكبا } هو الذي يحشر على وجهه إلى النار ومن { يمشى سويا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah is Meccan and has forty-four verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآيها أربع وأربعون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʾala sāʾil means that a caller invoked or requested an impending punishment; the bāʾ marks asking for it.
rows.anchor: أي دعا داع به بمعنى استدعاه ولذلك عدى الفعل بالباء

rows.speaker: النضر بن الحارث
rows.claim: One view identifies the asker as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who mocked the warning by quoting a challenge for stones from heaven in 8:32.
rows.anchor: والسائل هو النضر بن الحارث فإنه قال إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the asker as Abū Jahl, who mockingly demanded a fragment of the sky fall on them in 26:187.
rows.anchor: أو أبو جهل فإنه قال فأسقط علينا كسفا من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Messenger himself asked that their punishment be hastened.
rows.anchor: أو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام استعجل بعذابهم

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read sāla; it may mean “asked” in Quraysh usage, as illustrated by a line from Hudhayl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر « سال» وهو إما من السؤال على لغة قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sāla derives from flowing; the variant sāla sayl treats sayl as a verbal noun for “one who flows,” so a torrent flowed bearing punishment.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده أنه قرىء «سال سيل» على أن السيل مصدر بمعنى السائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense signals certainty: the punishment occurred at Badr in this world or will occur as the Fire in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ومضى الفعل لتحقق وقوعه إما في الدنيا وهو قتل بدر أو في الآخرة وهو عذاب النار
